newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Griffin oil field halts output owing to weather.
newsitem.headline: Griffin oil field halts output owing to weather.

text.p: The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd has halted crude oil output at the Australian offshore Griffin oil field because of a tropical low weather formation, industry sources said on Thursday.
The sources said the field was preparing to disconnect the floating production platform to move out of the path of the approaching storm.
However, a final decision on whether to disconnect or not would not be made until later in the day, industry sources said.
The nearby Cossack oil field was shut down earlier in the day because of the storm, a spokeswoman for operator Woodside Petroleum Ltd said.
Cossack was currently producing at a reduced rate of 65,000 barrels per day. It was preparing to disconnect to avoid the path of the storm, the spokeswoman said.

Cossack partners are units of BHP, British Petroleum Co Plc, Japan Australia LNG (MiMi) Pty Ltd -- a partnership of Mitsui & Co Ltd and Mitsubishi Corp -- Chevron Corp, Royal Dutch/Shell and Woodside.
BHP holds a 45-percent stake in the 80,000 bpd Griffin field, Mobil Corp 35 percent and Inpex Alpha Ltd 20 percent.
The two fields are off western Australia.
A tropical low about 400 kms northwest of the coastal town of Karratha and was expected to build into a cyclone, the Bureau of Meteorology said.
